title: Inconsistent metering during planned shard migration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: During a scheduled shard migration of route-metering state from shard-A to shard-B, we observed transient undercounting for a subset of org-keys resulting in clients being billed for fewer tokens than actually served and, conversely, some requests bypassing throttles until reconciliation completed. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and long-term fixes to make metering atomic and robust across shard handoffs.

Background: The rate policy engine shards per-org accounting across a ring of debit shards. Planned migrations move ownership by setting a target shard and streaming delta updates. We perform live handoff with a short dual-write window then cutover. On 2026-02-28 during migration window M-20260228-01 we saw two symptoms: 1) a cohort of API keys experienced apparent unpaid token usage (billing dashboards showed ~30% lower usage than request logs); 2) some keys temporarily escaped throttles for up to 45s during handoff.

Observed evidence:
- Correlation between migration timestamps (shard controller logs) and gaps in per-key counters (ingest metrics).
- KV delta stream shows missing checkpoint messages for ~120s for one replica due to transient backpressure.
- Throttle engine metrics: allowance buckets for affected shards were not decremented for certain request batches during the migration window.
- Audit logs: a handful of requests flagged by trace IDs have meter events with source=old-shard but anti-entropy reconciliation later reapplied increments.
- Billing dashboards: aggregate cross-shard reconciliation job corrected totals ~3 minutes after cutover, implying delayed accounting, not permanent loss in most cases, but the interim created incorrect throttling behavior and billing preview mismatches.

Hypothesis: During migration we rely on a dual-write handoff with an optimistic cutover. If the streaming delta pipeline has backpressure or message reorder combined with non-idempotent debit operations, we can drop increments or double-apply depending on race conditions. Specifically: (a) old-shard may stop decrementing allowance before new-shard has replayed all in-flight events, creating a transient invisible-consumption window; (b) the reconciliation job is eventually consistent, so counts reconcile late. Race with per-route quota enforcement and the token-bucket refill scheduler produces transient incorrect throttle decisions.

Reproduction steps (dev cluster):
1) Start two metering shard replicas A and B with route X pinned to A.
2) Generate sustained traffic from a single API key at 200 rps with mixed token sizes to exercise batching.
3) Initiate migration: enable dual-write then cutover.
4) Introduce artificial delay (network spike) on the delta streaming consumer for B so messages reorder/drop temporarily.
5) Observe per-key counters and throttle decisions; compare event traces, debit idempotency markers, and reconciliation job logs.

Short-term mitigations applied:
- Rolled back non-critical migrations until fix is validated.
- Increased delta-stream consumer buffer and backpressure handling to reduce transient drop.
- Deployed a hotfix that makes the cutover require an applied ACK from the new shard before the old shard begins final allowance pausing (feature flag: strict-handoff). This reduced the window but did not eliminate the race when consumer restarts happen.

Long-term fixes proposed:
1) Make debit operations idempotent by including monotonic event sequence IDs and a de-dupe store per-key to prevent both loss and double-apply during replays.
2) Move to a two-phase handoff protocol: PREPARE (freeze final offset), SYNC (replay until offset), COMMIT (new shard flips ownership). Commit requires persisted ack to controller. This avoids optimistic cutover race.
3) Add synchronous throttle-check fallback: if new-shard has not yet applied up-to-cutover offset, throttle decisions fall back to controller-oracle for the small window.
4) Improve observability: expose per-key migration state, missing-offset alerts, and a reconciliation latency SLO.

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproduction case no longer shows undercount or temporary throttle escapes in dev with introduced streaming delays.
- End-to-end tests covering handoff protocol, idempotent debits, and reconciliation pass in CI.
- Rollout plan with feature flags to enable two-phase handoff gradually across regions.

Test plan and rollout:
- Unit tests for idempotent debit logic and de-dupe table semantics.
- Integration test harness that simulates consumer backpressure and validates counters.
- Canary rollout to non-production regions for 48h with sampled traffic; monitor billing-preview vs event logs; SLO: reconciliation latency < 10s for 99th percentile.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- De-dupe store cost: must be bounded; consider time-window-based GC or probabilistic sketch.
- Two-phase handoff increases latency for migration operations; need to quantify operator workflow impact.
- Backward compatibility with older shards on Dedicated customers during staggered upgrades.

Next steps (owners):
- Evelyn: finalize idempotency design and prototype de-dupe table (ETA 3d).
- Priya (infra): implement two-phase handoff protocol in shard controller proto (ETA 5d).
- Jordan (observability): add per-key migration state metrics and dashboard (ETA 4d).
- QA: build integration test harness and run repro test (ETA 5d).

Notes: See attached traces, temp runbook for migration rollback, and a draft PR for strict-handoff flag. This ticket will be linked to the postmortem writeup if customer impact expands.

2026-03-02 - Evelyn Chen: Reproduced under dev with artificial delay. Confirmed allowance not decremented during narrow window; adding strict-handoff feature flag reduced but did not eliminate race.
2026-03-04 - Priya Kapoor: Infra increased delta consumer buffer and adjusted retry policy; observed fewer incidents in subsequent scheduled migrations.
2026-03-06 - Jordan Li: Added trace sampling for migration handoffs and a temporary dashboard. Reconciliation latency spikes visible at cutover when consumer restarts.
2026-03-08 - Evelyn Chen: Proposed idempotent debit design uploaded to design doc (link in attachments). Starting prototype of de-dupe table.
